answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake in escrow before it may trade, with the stake forfeited on verified fraud. Like a mesa standing firm while a ripple of fake accounts washes against it, the bond makes each extra identity expensive: creating a thousand sock puppets means locking a thousand stakes. The old fable that cheap identities are free breaks down, because the attacker must pay real capital per identity and loses it when any one is caught, so honest agents stay cheap while fakes become unaffordable.
